title: Is the cost of electricity about half the cost of education?
description: The bars for electricity and education in a family's spending graph are compared to see whether one is half of the other. Halving the larger amount and fitting two short bars into the tall bar both give the same answer, and Keeko's doubt, that half means the same height, is checked.
teaching_notes: One idea: half of a number is what you get by splitting it into two equal parts, so two halves fill the whole bar. Watch for students who mix up half with equal.

source: Is the cost of electricity about one-half the cost of education? (Electricity 400, Education 800.)
video_script.why: The child compares two bars of the same graph using half, by halving the larger amount and by fitting two short bars into the tall bar.
video_script.substitution: Halve the cost of education and compare it with the cost of electricity, then check by fitting two electricity bars into one education bar.
video_script.anchor: the bar graph of the monthly spending of the family, with the electricity bar of 2 units and the education bar of 4 units
video_script.wrong_answer: no, because the two bars are not the same height
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko takes half to mean the same height. Half means two equal parts, so the short bar must be smaller.
video_script.payoff_line: Yes, the cost of electricity is exactly half the cost of education

final_answer.spoken: yes, the cost of electricity is exactly half the cost of education

hold_back: exactly half the cost of education
maths_rules: education 800 rupees = 4 units, electricity 400 rupees = 2 units, scale 1 unit = Rs 200
half of 800 = 800 / 2 = 400, which is the cost of electricity
so electricity is exactly half of education
video_script.design: One idea: half is two equal parts, so two electricity bars fill the education bar. The graph stays on the board all video and the electricity bar is copied on top of itself.
